newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Currency board seen reviving Bulgaria stock market.
newsitem.headline: Currency board seen reviving Bulgaria stock market.

text.p: Bulgaria's planned introduction of a currency board is expected to revive the country's stock market, Bulgarian Stock Exchange (BSE) executive director Viktor Papazov said on Thursday.
Papazov attributed declining stock trade to delayed privatisation and the destruction of public confidence in the lev and government securities.

"If a currency board is introduced the stock exchange could become a serious source of cash from abroad. Shares of enterprises offered for privatisation can be traded there at prices set by the market," Papazov told a news conference.

Under the rules of the proposed currency board, levs in circulation would have to be matched by central bank foreign exchange reserves -- a mechanism aimed at removing political pressure on the bank to print money.
However, Papazov said the currency board would not solve Bulgaria's grave economic problems unless the government stepped up privatisation and closed loss-making enterprises.
He said many big western investment funds had shown interest in diversifying their portfolios with Bulgarian shares once the stock market guaranteed transparent trading rules.
Bulgaria's Securities and Stock Exchange Commission (SSEC) suspended exchange floor trading in October after companies failed to meet legal requirements.
Altogether 19 companies with 28 issues were quoted on the SSEC exchange floors, of which four companies with 10 issues actually traded.

The BSE was set up last year after the merger of the First Bulgarian Stock Exchange, which was the first to introduce listing requirements, the Sofia Stock Exchange, the Black Sea Stock exchange, and the stock exchanges in Plovdiv, Rousse and Veliko Turnovo.
The BSE will be licensed by the SSEC once it collects the required 100 million lev capital. It has so far collected 72 million levs, said Papazov.

The currency board is expected to be introduced early next year with support from the International Monetary Fund after parliament approves the 1997 budget and the necessary legal amendments to make the system operational.
